title.raw: 卷八十 列傳第四十 孝武十四王 Volume 80 Biographies 40: Xiaowu Shisi Wang

sentences.zh: 孝武帝二十八男：文穆皇后生廢帝子業、豫章王子尚，陳淑媛生晉安王子勛，阮容華生安陸王子綏，徐昭容生皇子子深，何淑儀生松滋侯子房，史昭華生臨海王子頊，殷貴妃生始平孝敬王子鸞，次永嘉王子仁，與皇子子深同生，何婕妤生皇子子鳳，謝昭容生始安王子真，江婕妤生皇子子玄，史昭儀生邵陵王子元，次齊敬王子羽，與始平孝敬王子鸞同生，江美人生皇子子衡，楊婕妤生淮南王子孟，次皇子子況，與皇子子玄同生，次南平王子產，與永嘉王子仁同生，次晉陵孝王子雲，次皇子子文，並與始平孝敬王子鸞同生，次廬陵王子輿，與淮南王子孟同生，次南海哀王子師，與始平孝敬王子鸞同生，次淮陽思王子霄，與皇子子玄同生，次皇子子雍，與始安王子真同生，次皇子子趨，與皇子子鳳同生，次皇子子期，與皇子子衡同生，次東平王子嗣，與始安王子真同生，杜容華生皇子子悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu had twenty-eight sons: Empress Wenmu bore the Deposed Emperor Ziye and Yuzhang Prince Zi Shang; Lady Chen bore Jin'an Prince Zi Xun; Ruan Ronghua bore Anlu Prince Zi Sui; Xu Zhaorong bore Prince Zi Shen; He Shuyi bore Songzi Marquis Zi Fang; Shi Zhaohua bore Linhai Prince Zi Xu; Noble Consort Yin bore Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, next Yongjia Prince Zi Ren, born together with Prince Zi Shen; Lady He bore Prince Zi Feng; Xie Zhaorong bore Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen; Lady Jiang bore Prince Zi Xuan; Lady Shi bore Shaoling Prince Zi Yuan, next Qi Jing Prince Zi Yu, born together with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan; Lady Jiang bore Prince Zi Heng; Lady Yang bore Huainan Prince Zi Meng, next Prince Zi Kuang, born together with Prince Zi Xuan, next Nanping Prince Zi Chan, born together with Yongjia Prince Zi Ren, next Jinling Xiao Prince Zi Yun, next Prince Zi Wen, all born together with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, next Luling Prince Zi Yu, born together with Huainan Prince Zi Meng, next Nanhai Ai Prince Zi Shi, born together with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, next Huaiyang Si Prince Zi Xiao, born together with Prince Zi Xuan, next Prince Zi Yong, born together with Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen, next Prince Zi Qu, born together with Prince Zi Feng, next Prince Zi Qi, born together with Prince Zi Heng, next Dongping Prince Zi Si, born together with Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen; Du Ronghua bore Prince Zi Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu had twenty-eight sons. Empress Wenmu bore the Deposed Emperor Ziye and Yuzhang Prince Zi Shang. Lady Chen bore Jin'an Prince Zi Xun. Ruan Ronghua bore Anlu Prince Zi Sui. Xu Zhaorong bore Prince Zi Shen. He Shuyi bore Songzi Marquis Zi Fang. Shi Zhaohua bore Linhai Prince Zi Xu. Noble Consort Yin bore Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, then Yongjia Prince Zi Ren (twins with Prince Zi Shen). Lady He bore Prince Zi Feng. Xie Zhaorong bore Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen. Lady Jiang bore Prince Zi Xuan. Lady Shi bore Shaoling Prince Zi Yuan, then Qi Jing Prince Zi Yu (twins with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan). Lady Jiang bore Prince Zi Heng. Lady Yang bore Huainan Prince Zi Meng, then Prince Zi Kuang (twins with Prince Zi Xuan), then Nanping Prince Zi Chan (twins with Yongjia Prince Zi Ren), then Jinling Xiao Prince Zi Yun and Prince Zi Wen (all twins with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan), then Luling Prince Zi Yu (twins with Huainan Prince Zi Meng), then Nanhai Ai Prince Zi Shi (twins with Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan), then Huaiyang Si Prince Zi Xiao (twins with Prince Zi Xuan), then Prince Zi Yong (twins with Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen), then Prince Zi Qu (twins with Prince Zi Feng), then Prince Zi Qi (twins with Prince Zi Heng), then Dongping Prince Zi Si (twins with Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen). Du Ronghua bore Prince Zi Yue.

sentences.zh: 安陸王子綏、南平王子產、廬陵王子輿並出繼。

translations.literal: Anlu Prince Zi Sui, Nanping Prince Zi Chan, and Luling Prince Zi Yu were all adopted out as heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Anlu Prince Zi Sui, Nanping Prince Zi Chan, and Luling Prince Zi Yu were all given in adoption to continue other lines.

sentences.zh: 皇子子深、子鳳、子玄、子衡、子況、子文、子雍未封，早夭。

translations.literal: Princes Zi Shen, Zi Feng, Zi Xuan, Zi Heng, Zi Kuang, Zi Wen, and Zi Yong received no fiefs and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Zi Shen, Zi Feng, Zi Xuan, Zi Heng, Zi Kuang, Zi Wen, and Zi Yong were never enfeoffed and died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 子趨、子期、子悅未封，為明帝所殺。

translations.literal: Zi Qu, Zi Qi, and Zi Yue received no fiefs and were killed by Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Qu, Zi Qi, and Zi Yue had received no fiefs when Emperor Ming had them put to death.

sentences.zh: 豫章王

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang

sentences.zh: 豫章王子尚字孝師，孝武帝第二子也。

translations.literal: Yuzhang Prince Zi Shang, style Xiaoshi, was the second son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhang Prince Zi Shang, whose style name was Xiaoshi, was Emperor Xiaowu's second son.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，年六歲，封西陽王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian, at age six, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiyang with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xiaojian era, when he was six, he was made Prince of Xiyang with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 仍都督南徐兗二州諸軍事、北中郎將、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was also made Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the two provinces Southern Xu and Yan, Northern Central Army General, and Governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time he was appointed to command the armies of Southern Xu and Yan, with the titles Northern Central Army General and Governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷揚州刺史。

translations.literal: That same year he was transferred to Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was reassigned as Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he received the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 三年，分浙江西立王畿，以浙江東為揚州，命子尚都督揚州江州之鄱陽晉安建安三郡諸軍事、揚州刺史，將軍如故，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the third year, the region west of the Zhe River was set apart as the royal domain, and the region east of the Zhe River was made Yangzhou; Zi Shang was ordered to command the military affairs of Yangzhou and the three commanderies Poyang, Jin'an, and Jian'an of Jiangzhou, as Governor of Yangzhou, his generalship unchanged, and was granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the court carved out the lands west of the Zhe River as the royal domain and made the eastern bank Yangzhou. Zi Shang was ordered to command Yangzhou and Jiangzhou's Poyang, Jin'an, and Jian'an commanderies, retaining his general's rank as Governor of Yangzhou, and was granted a full ensemble of martial music.

sentences.zh: 五年，改封豫章王，戶邑如先，領會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang, his household fief as before, and he took charge as Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his title was changed to Prince of Yuzhang with the same fief as before, and he served concurrently as Governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 七年，加使持節，進號車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was given the credential Staff of Authority and promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he received the Staff of Authority and was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 其年，又加散騎常侍，以本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: That same year he was also made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and, under his existing title, was given the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was further named Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and, while keeping his existing rank, was granted an establishment with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 時東土大旱，鄞縣多疁田，世祖使子尚上表至鄞縣勸農。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern lands suffered great drought; Yin County had many terraced fields; the Emperor had Zi Shang submit a memorial and go to Yin County to encourage agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern provinces were then in severe drought, and Yin County had extensive terraced fields. The Emperor sent Zi Shang to submit a memorial and travel to Yin County to promote farming.

sentences.zh: 又立左學，召生徒，置儒林祭酒一人，學生師敬，位比州治中；

translations.literal: He also established a left academy, summoned students, and appointed one Libationer of the Forest of Scholars, whom the students honored as teacher, with rank equal to a provincial aide;
translations.idiomatic: He also founded a left academy, enrolled students, and appointed a Libationer of the Forest of Scholars whom the students were to honor as their teacher, with rank comparable to a provincial aide;

sentences.zh: 文學祭酒一人，比西曹；

translations.literal: one Libationer of Letters, equal to the western bureau;
translations.idiomatic: one Libationer of Letters, equal in standing to the western bureau;

sentences.zh: 勸學從事二人，比祭酒從事。

translations.literal: two aides for encouraging study, equal to aides of the libationers.
translations.idiomatic: and two aides for encouraging study, each with rank comparable to an aide of the libationers.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，罷王畿復舊，徵子尚都督揚、南徐二州諸軍事，領尚書令，解督東揚州，餘如故。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor acceded, the royal domain was abolished and the old arrangements restored; Zi Shang was summoned to command the military affairs of Yang and Southern Xu, to head the Secretariat as Director, and was relieved of command over Eastern Yangzhou; the rest was as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, the royal domain was abolished and the old administrative divisions restored. Zi Shang was recalled to command Yang and Southern Xu, appointed Director of the Secretariat, and relieved of his authority over Eastern Yangzhou; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，孝建中，世祖以子尚太子母弟，上甚留心。

translations.literal: At first, during Xiaojian, because Zi Shang was the younger brother of the crown prince by the same mother, the Emperor paid him very close attention.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, during the Xiaojian era, the Emperor took a keen interest in Zi Shang because he was the crown prince's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 後新安王子鸞以母幸見愛，子尚之寵稍衰。

translations.literal: Later Xin'an Prince Zi Luan, because his mother enjoyed favor, came to be loved, and Zi Shang's favor gradually waned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xin'an Prince Zi Luan won the Emperor's affection through his mother's favor, and Zi Shang's standing gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 既長，人才凡劣，凶慝有廢帝風。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, his talent was altogether mediocre, and his vicious cruelty bore the manner of the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older, his abilities proved mediocre, and his cruelty matched the Deposed Emperor's character.

sentences.zh: 太宗殞廢帝，稱太皇后令曰：「子尚頑凶極悖，行乖天理。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming killed the Deposed Emperor, he issued an order in the name of the Grand Empress Dowager, saying: "Zi Shang is stubbornly vicious to the utmost and utterly perverse; his conduct violates Heaven's principle.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming killed the Deposed Emperor, he issued an edict in the Grand Empress Dowager's name: "Zi Shang is utterly stubborn and depraved, and his conduct defies Heaven's law.

sentences.zh: 楚玉淫亂縱慝，義絕人經。

translations.literal: Chuyu indulged in lewd disorder and unrestrained wickedness, severing all bonds of human morality.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyu has indulged in lewdness and unrestrained vice, breaking every bond of human decency.

sentences.zh: 並可於第賜盡。

translations.literal: Both may be granted death at their residences."
translations.idiomatic: Let both be granted death in their own residences."

sentences.zh: 」子尚時年十六。

translations.literal: Zi Shang was then sixteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Shang was sixteen at the time.

sentences.zh: 楚玉，山陰公主也。

translations.literal: Chuyu was the Princess of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyu was the Princess of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 廢帝改封為會稽郡長公主，食湯沐邑二千戶，給鼓吹一部，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor changed her enfeoffment to Grand Princess of Kuaiji commandery, with a bath-and-fief estate of two thousand households, granted one set of martial music, and twenty armed attendants with ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor re-enfeoffed her as Grand Princess of Kuaiji, with a fief of two thousand households for her upkeep, a full ensemble of martial music, and twenty armed attendants bearing ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 未及拜受而廢帝敗。

translations.literal: Before she could receive the investiture, the Deposed Emperor fell.
translations.idiomatic: She had not yet received the investiture when the Deposed Emperor was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 楚玉肆情淫縱，以尚書吏部郎褚淵貌美，請自侍十日，廢帝許之。

translations.literal: Chuyu indulged her passions without restraint; because Chu Yuan of the Secretariat's Ministry of Personnel was handsome, she asked to keep him in attendance for ten days, and the Deposed Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyu gave free rein to her lust. Finding Chu Yuan of the Secretariat's Ministry of Personnel handsome, she asked to keep him in attendance for ten days, and the Deposed Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 淵雖承旨而行，以死自固，楚玉不能制也。

translations.literal: Although Yuan complied with the order in outward action, he held firm even unto death, and Chuyu could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan outwardly obeyed the order but held himself firm even at the risk of death, and Chuyu could not prevail over him.

sentences.zh: 晉安王

translations.literal: Prince of Jin'an
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin'an

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勛字孝德，孝武帝第三子也。

translations.literal: Jin'an Prince Zi Xun, style Xiaode, was the third son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin'an Prince Zi Xun, whose style name was Xiaode, was Emperor Xiaowu's third son.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，年五歲，封晉安王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming, at age five, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin'an with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming, when he was five, he was made Prince of Jin'an with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 仍都督南兗州徐州之東海諸軍事、征虜將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was also made Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Southern Yan and Donghai of Xuzhou, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was simultaneously appointed to command Southern Yan and Xuzhou's Donghai commandery, with the titles General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 七年，改督江州南豫州之晉熙新蔡郢州之西陽三郡諸軍事、前將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his command was changed to the military affairs of Jiangzhou, Jinxing and Xincai of Southern Yuzhou, and Xiyang of Yingzhou—three commanderies—as Forward General and Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year his command was shifted to Jiangzhou, Southern Yuzhou's Jinxing and Xincai, and Yingzhou's Xiyang, with the titles Forward General and Governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷使持節、都督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵隨二郡諸軍事、鎮軍將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the four provinces Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, and Southern Qin and the two commanderies Jingling and Sui of Yingzhou, General Who Pacifies the Army, Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians, and Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was reassigned as Bearer of the Staff of Authority to command Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, and Southern Qin, along with Yingzhou's Jingling and Sui, with the titles General Who Pacifies the Army, Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians, and Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 未拜而世祖崩，以鎮軍將軍還為江州，本官如故。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the appointment the Emperor died; as General Who Pacifies the Army he returned to Jiangzhou, his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the new post, the Emperor died. He returned to Jiangzhou as General Who Pacifies the Army, retaining his previous titles.

sentences.zh: 眼患風，為世祖所不愛。

translations.literal: His eyes suffered from wind ailment, and the Emperor did not favor him.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered from an eye ailment, and the Emperor did not favor him.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，加使持節。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he was given the Staff of Authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe he received the Staff of Authority.

sentences.zh: 時廢帝狂凶，多所誅害。

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor was mad and vicious and put many to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was then violently deranged and executed many people.

sentences.zh: 前撫軍諮議參軍何邁少好武，頗招集才力之士。

translations.literal: Former Adviser to the Army Who Pacifies the Army He Mai had from youth loved martial affairs and gathered many men of strength and talent.
translations.idiomatic: He Mai, formerly an adviser on the staff of the General Who Pacifies the Army, had loved martial pursuits since youth and gathered many men of strength and ability.

sentences.zh: 邁先尚太祖女新蔡公主，帝詐云主薨，殺宮人代之，顯加殯葬，而納主於後宮。

translations.literal: Mai had earlier married the Grand Princess of Xincai, daughter of Emperor Taizu; the Emperor falsely announced that the princess had died, killed a palace woman to replace her, gave her a conspicuous funeral, and took the princess into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Mai had earlier married the Grand Princess of Xincai, a daughter of Emperor Taizu. The Emperor falsely announced her death, killed a palace woman to stand in for her at the funeral, staged a public burial, and took the princess into his inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 深忌邁，邁慮禍及，謀因帝出行為變，迎立子勛。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply resented Mai; Mai feared disaster would reach him and plotted to stage a coup when the Emperor went out on tour and install Zi Xun as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor deeply hated Mai. Fearing for his life, Mai plotted to raise a coup when the Emperor traveled abroad and install Zi Xun on the throne.

sentences.zh: 事泄，帝自率宿衞兵誅邁，使八座奏子勛與邁通謀。

translations.literal: When the plot leaked, the Emperor personally led the palace guard to execute Mai and had the Eight Excellencies memorialize that Zi Xun had conspired with Mai.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, the Emperor personally led the palace guard to execute Mai and had the Eight Excellencies report that Zi Xun had conspired with him.

sentences.zh: 又手詔子勛曰：「何邁殺我立汝，汝自計孰若孝武邪？

translations.literal: He also sent a personal edict to Zi Xun, saying: "He Mai would kill me to set you up. Do you reckon yourself the equal of Emperor Xiaowu?
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Zi Xun a personal edict: "He Mai means to kill me and put you on the throne. Do you truly think yourself the equal of Emperor Xiaowu?

sentences.zh: 可自為其所。

translations.literal: You may act as you see fit for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Do as you think best for yourself."

sentences.zh: 」遣左右朱景雲送藥賜子勛死。

translations.literal: He sent his attendant Zhu Jingyun to deliver poison and grant Zi Xun death.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his attendant Zhu Jingyun with poison to grant Zi Xun death.

sentences.zh: 景雲至盆口，停不進，遣信使報長史鄧琬。

translations.literal: Jingyun reached Penkou, halted and did not advance, and sent a messenger to report to Chief Administrator Deng Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyun reached Penkou, halted without advancing, and sent a messenger to inform Chief Administrator Deng Wan.

sentences.zh: 琬等因奉子勛起兵，以廢立為名。

translations.literal: Wan and the others thereupon raised troops in support of Zi Xun, taking deposition and enthronement as their rallying cry.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and his colleagues then raised troops in Zi Xun's name, proclaiming their cause the removal of a tyrant and the enthronement of a legitimate ruler.

sentences.zh: 太宗定亂，進子勛號車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming settled the turmoil, he advanced Zi Xun's title to General of Chariots and Cavalry with an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming restored order, he promoted Zi Xun to General of Chariots and Cavalry with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 琬等不受命，傳檄京邑。

translations.literal: Wan and the others refused the order and circulated a proclamation to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and his allies refused to obey and circulated a proclamation to the capital.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月七日，奉子勛為帝，即偽位於尋陽城，年號義嘉元年，備置百官，四方並響應，威震天下。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the first month of the second year of Taishi, they enthroned Zi Xun as emperor; he immediately took the false throne at Xunyang city, with the era name Yijia, year one; fully appointed the hundred officials; all quarters responded together; his prestige shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the first month of the second year of Taishi they proclaimed Zi Xun emperor. He took the rebel throne at Xunyang, adopted the era name Yijia, appointed a full bureaucracy, and drew responses from every quarter until his power seemed to shake the realm.

sentences.zh: 是歲四方貢計，並詣尋陽。

translations.literal: That year the tribute tallies from the four quarters all went to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: That year the provincial tribute reports from across the realm were all sent to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 遣左衞將軍孫沖之等下據赭圻，又遣豫州刺史劉胡率大眾來屯鵲尾，又遣安北將軍袁顗總統眾軍。

translations.literal: He sent Left Guards General Sun Chongzhi and others downstream to hold Zheqi, also sent Governor of Yuzhou Liu Hu leading a great host to encamp at Quewei, and also sent General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Yi to command all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Left Guards General Sun Chongzhi and others to seize Zheqi downstream, dispatched Governor of Yuzhou Liu Hu with a large force to encamp at Quewei, and appointed General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Yi supreme commander of the armies.

sentences.zh: 臺軍屯據錢谿，斷顗等糧援，胡遣將攻之，大敗，於是焚營遁走。

translations.literal: The imperial armies encamped at Qianxi, cutting off Yuan and the others' grain supplies; Hu sent generals to attack them, suffered a great defeat, and thereupon burned the camps and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armies held Qianxi and cut off Yuan Yi's supply lines. Liu Hu sent generals to attack them but was routed and burned his camps before fleeing.

sentences.zh: 顗聞胡去，亦棄眾南奔。

translations.literal: When Yi heard that Hu had gone, he too abandoned his troops and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yi learned that Liu Hu had fled, he too abandoned his army and fled south.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之諸軍至尋陽，誅子勛及其母，同逆皆夷滅。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's armies reached Xunyang, they executed Zi Xun and his mother, and all who shared the rebellion were exterminated to the last.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi's armies reached Xunyang, they executed Zi Xun and his mother and exterminated all who had joined the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 子勛死時年十一，即葬尋陽廬山。

translations.literal: Zi Xun was eleven when he died and was buried immediately on Mount Lu at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Xun was eleven when he died and was buried at once on Mount Lu near Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 松滋侯

translations.literal: Marquis of Songzi
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Songzi

sentences.zh: 松滋侯子房字孝良，孝武帝第六子也。

translations.literal: Songzi Marquis Zi Fang, style Xiaoliang, was the sixth son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Songzi Marquis Zi Fang, whose style name was Xiaoliang, was Emperor Xiaowu's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，年五歲，封尋陽王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming, at age five, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xunyang with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming, when he was five, he was made Prince of Xunyang with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 仍為冠軍將軍、淮南宣城二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was also made Champion General and Governor of the two commanderies Huainan and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was simultaneously appointed Champion General and Governor of Huainan and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷豫州刺史，將軍、淮南太守如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Governor of Yuzhou; his generalship and governorship of Huainan were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was reassigned as Governor of Yuzhou while retaining his rank as general and his post as Governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 六年，改領宣城太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed to take charge as Governor of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was reassigned to govern Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 七年，進號右將軍，解宣城，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was advanced to General of the Right and relieved of Xuancheng; the rest was as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to General of the Right and relieved of Xuancheng; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝永光元年，遷東揚州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongguang under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was transferred to Governor of Eastern Yangzhou; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongguang under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was reassigned as Governor of Eastern Yangzhou while keeping his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，罷東揚州，子房以本號督會稽東陽新安臨海永嘉五郡諸軍事、會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe Eastern Yangzhou was abolished; Zi Fang, under his existing title, was made to command the military affairs of the five commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, and was Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe Eastern Yangzhou was abolished. Zi Fang retained his existing rank while being appointed to command Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, and to serve as Governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，改督為都督，進號安東將軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, his command was changed from supervisor to commander-in-chief, he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East, and his governorship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Zi Fang's supervisory command was elevated to full commandership, he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East, and he retained his post as governor.

sentences.zh: 又徵為撫軍，領太常。

translations.literal: He was also summoned as General Who Pacifies the Army and concurrently headed the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was also recalled to serve as General Who Pacifies the Army and concurrently as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 長史孔覬不受命，舉兵反，應晉安王。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Kong Xian refused the order, raised troops in rebellion, and responded to Jin'an Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Kong Xian refused to obey, raised troops in revolt, and rallied to Jin'an Prince.

sentences.zh: 子勛即偽位，進子房號車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Zi Xun took the false throne, he advanced Zi Fang's title to General of Chariots and Cavalry with an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi Xun took the rebel throne, he promoted Zi Fang to General of Chariots and Cavalry with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 三吳晉陵並受命於覬。

translations.literal: The Three Wu regions and Jinling all accepted orders from Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wu commanderies and Jinling all submitted to Kong Xian's authority.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣衞將軍巴陵王休若督諸將吳喜等東討，戰無不捷，以次平定。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Guards General Prince of Baling Xiu Ruo to command the generals Wu Xi and others in an eastern campaign; in battle they were never unsuccessful, and the regions were pacified in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Guards General Prince of Baling Xiu Ruo to lead generals including Wu Xi in an eastern campaign. They won every battle and pacified the region step by step.

sentences.zh: 上虞令王晏起兵殺覬，囚子房，送還京都，上宥之，貶為松滋縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shangyu Wang Yan raised troops, killed Xian, imprisoned Zi Fang, and sent him back to the capital; the Emperor pardoned him and demoted him to Marquis of Songzi county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyu Magistrate Wang Yan raised troops, killed Kong Xian, imprisoned Zi Fang, and sent him to the capital. The Emperor spared his life but demoted him to Marquis of Songzi with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 司徒建安王休仁以子房兄弟終為禍難，勸上除之。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren, considering that Zi Fang and his brothers would in the end bring calamity, urged the Emperor to eliminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren argued that Zi Fang and his brothers would ultimately bring disaster and urged the Emperor to eliminate them.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「不虞之釁，著自終古，情為法屈，聖達是遵。

translations.literal: He thereupon issued an edict, saying: "Unforeseen calamities have been manifest from antiquity; affection yields to law—this the sage and enlightened follow.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "Unforeseen disasters have been known since antiquity. Even affection must yield to law—this is what the sage ruler follows.

sentences.zh: 朕埽穢定傾，再全寶業，遠惟鴻基，猥當負荷。

translations.literal: We have swept away filth and stabilized the tipping vessel, twice restoring the precious enterprise; reflecting far on the great foundation, we unworthily bear its weight.
translations.idiomatic: We have swept away corruption and righted the tottering state, twice restoring the imperial enterprise. Contemplating the great foundation laid by our forebears, we unworthily bear its weight.

sentences.zh: 思弘治道，務盡敦睦，而妖豎遘扇，妄造異圖。

translations.literal: We wished to expand the way of governance and exhaust all bonds of kinship, yet demonic villains encountered and fanned rebellion, recklessly forging alien designs.
translations.idiomatic: We sought to broaden the path of good government and nurture every bond of kinship, yet wicked men have stirred rebellion and recklessly plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 自西南阻兵，東夏侵斥，都邸羣凶，密相脣齒。

translations.literal: Since the southwest blocked with arms and the eastern summer lands were invaded and seized, the villains at the capital lodges were secretly lip-to-tooth with one another.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion has blocked the southwest and encroached on the eastern provinces, while villains in the capital have secretly acted in concert.

sentences.zh: 路休之兄弟，專作謀主，規興禍亂，令舍人嚴龍覘覦宮省，以羽林出討，宿衞單罄，候隙伺間，將謀竊發。

translations.literal: The brothers Lu Xiuzhi served exclusively as plot-masters, scheming to raise calamity and disorder; they ordered Attendant Yan Long to spy on the palace offices; with the Feathered Forest sent out on campaign, the night guard was utterly depleted; watching for gaps and awaiting opportunities, they were about to plot a stealthy rising.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Lu Xiuzhi served as chief conspirators, plotting to stir rebellion. They ordered Attendant Yan Long to spy on the palace. With the Feathered Forest guards sent on campaign, the night watch was left bare, and they waited for an opening to launch a coup.

sentences.zh: 劉祗在蕃，規相應援，通言北寇，引令過淮。

translations.literal: Liu Zhi was in his fief, planning mutual support in response, spreading word of northern invaders to draw them across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi, holding a princely fief, planned to lend support and spread reports of northern invasion to draw enemy forces across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 頃休範濟江，潛欲拒捍，賴卜祚靈長，姦回弗逞。

translations.literal: Recently Xiu Fan crossed the river; he secretly wished to resist and hold fast, but relying on the divined fortune's spiritual endurance, the treacherous and perverse could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu Fan recently crossed the Yangzi, he secretly sought to resist us, but Heaven's favor proved enduring and the traitors could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 陰慝已露，宜盡憲辟，實以方難未夷，曲加遵養。

translations.literal: Their hidden wickedness had already been exposed and they should fully have suffered the penalties of law, but in truth because regional troubles were not yet pacified, they were indulgently spared and nurtured.
translations.idiomatic: Their hidden crimes had been exposed and they deserved full punishment under the law, but because rebellion still raged in the provinces, we showed them undue forbearance.

sentences.zh: 今王化帖泰，宜辨忠邪，涓流不壅，燎火難滅。

translations.literal: Now the royal transforming influence is secure and tranquil; loyalty and treachery should be distinguished; if trickling streams are not dammed, prairie fires are hard to extinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Now that royal order is secure, loyalty and treachery must be distinguished. If trickling streams are not dammed, prairie fires cannot be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 便可委之有司，肅正刑典。

translations.literal: They may now be entrusted to the appropriate offices to enforce the penal code with solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Let them be handed over to the proper authorities to enforce the law with full rigor.

sentences.zh: 松滋侯子房等淪陷逆徒，協同醜悖，遂與籤帥羣小，潛通南釁，連結祗等，還圖朕躬。

translations.literal: Songzi Marquis Zi Fang and others fell in with the rebel band, collaborating in vile perversity; they then joined with petty commanders of divination lots and secretly communicated with the southern rebellion, linking with Zhi and the rest, and turned to plot against Our person.
translations.idiomatic: Songzi Marquis Zi Fang and others fell in with the rebels and joined their vile schemes. They conspired with petty military leaders, secretly communicated with the southern rebellion, allied with Liu Zhi and his associates, and plotted against us.

sentences.zh: 雖咎戾已彰，在法無宥，猶子之情，良所未忍。

translations.literal: Although their guilt was already manifest and under the law there was no pardon, the feeling toward a son was truly what we could not bear.
translations.idiomatic: Though their guilt was clear and the law allowed no mercy, the bond of father and son was more than we could bring ourselves to sever.

sentences.zh: 可廢為庶人，徙付遠郡。

translations.literal: They may be deposed to commoner status and relocated to distant commanderies."
translations.idiomatic: Let them be deposed to commoner status and exiled to distant commanderies."

sentences.zh: 」於是並殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: They were then all put to death.

sentences.zh: 子房時年十一。

translations.literal: Zi Fang was then eleven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Fang was eleven at the time.

sentences.zh: 路休之等以崇憲太后既崩，自慮將來不立，不自安。

translations.literal: Lu Xiuzhi and the others, because Empress Dowager Chongxian had already died, feared they would not be established in the future and were ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiuzhi and his associates, fearing that with Empress Dowager Chongxian dead they would lose their standing, grew uneasy about the future.

sentences.zh: 劉祗在南兗州，有志為逆。

translations.literal: Liu Zhi was in Southern Yan and had the will to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi, posted in Southern Yan, harbored rebellious ambitions.

sentences.zh: 嚴龍，太祖元嘉中，已為中書舍人、南臺御史，世祖又以為舍人，甚見委信。

translations.literal: Yan Long, already during Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, had served as Secretariat Attendant and Censor of the Southern Terrace; the Emperor again made him an attendant and greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Long had already served under Emperor Taizu during the Yuanjia era as Secretariat Attendant and Censor of the Southern Terrace. Emperor Xiaowu reappointed him as an attendant and placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 景和、泰始之際，至越騎校尉，右軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the transition between Jinghe and Taishi he reached Colonel of the Upland Cavalry and General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: By the transition from Jinghe to Taishi he had risen to Colonel of the Upland Cavalry and General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 至是懷異端，故及於誅。

translations.literal: By then he harbored alien designs, and therefore met execution.
translations.idiomatic: By then he harbored treacherous designs and was therefore executed.

sentences.zh: 臨海王

translations.literal: Prince of Linhai
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Linhai

sentences.zh: 臨海王子頊字孝列，孝武帝第七子也。

translations.literal: Linhai Prince Zi Xu, style Xiaolie, was the seventh son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Linhai Prince Zi Xu, whose style name was Xiaolie, was Emperor Xiaowu's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，年五歲，封歷陽王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming, at age five, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liyang with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming, when he was five, he was made Prince of Liyang with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 仍為冠軍將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: He was also made Champion General and Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was simultaneously appointed Champion General and Governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 五年，改封臨海王，戶邑如先。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Linhai, his household fief as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his title was changed to Prince of Linhai with the same fief as before.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷使持節、都督廣交二州湘州之始興始安臨賀三郡諸軍事、征虜將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: That same year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the two provinces Guang and Jiao and the three commanderies Shixing, Shi'an, and Linhe of Xiangzhou, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Central Army General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was reassigned as Bearer of the Staff of Authority to command Guang and Jiao, along with Xiangzhou's Shixing, Shi'an, and Linhe, with the titles General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Central Army General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未之鎮，徙荊州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post he was moved to Governor of Jingzhou; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the post he was reassigned as Governor of Jingzhou while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 八年，進號前將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Forward General.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，以本號都督荊、湘、雍、益、梁、寧、南北秦八州諸軍事，刺史如故。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor acceded, under his existing title he was made Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the eight provinces Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, Northern Qin, and Southern Qin; his governorship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, Zi Xu retained his existing rank while being appointed to command Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, Northern Qin, and Southern Qin; his post as governor remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，解督雍州，以為鎮軍將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, he was relieved of command over Yong and made General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Zi Xu was relieved of his command over Yong and appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 尋留本任，進督雍州，又進號平西將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he retained his original duties, was advanced to command Yong, and was further promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retained his original post, was given command over Yong, and was further promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 長史孔道存不受命，舉兵反，以應晉安王子勛。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Kong Daocun refused the order, raised troops in rebellion, and responded to Jin'an Prince Zi Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Kong Daocun refused to obey, raised troops in revolt, and rallied to Jin'an Prince Zi Xun.

sentences.zh: 子勛即偽位，進號衞將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Zi Xun took the false throne, he advanced his title to Guards General with an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi Xun took the rebel throne, he promoted Zi Xu to Guards General with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 鵲尾奔敗，吳喜、張興世等軍至，子頊賜死，時年十一。

translations.literal: When Quewei fell in rout, the armies of Wu Xi, Zhang Xingshi, and others arrived; Zi Xu was granted death; he was then eleven years old.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Quewei, the armies of Wu Xi, Zhang Xingshi, and others arrived. Zi Xu was ordered to take his own life. He was eleven at the time.

sentences.zh: 葬巴陵。

translations.literal: He was buried at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Baling.

sentences.zh: 始平王

translations.literal: Prince of Shiping
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shiping

sentences.zh: 始平孝敬王子鸞字孝羽，孝武帝第八子也。

translations.literal: Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, style Xiaoyu, was the eighth son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiping Xiaojing Prince Zi Luan, whose style name was Xiaoyu, was Emperor Xiaowu's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，年五歲，封襄陽王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming, at age five, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangyang with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming, when he was five, he was made Prince of Xiangyang with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 仍為東中郎將、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He was also made Eastern Central Army General and Governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was simultaneously appointed Eastern Central Army General and Governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 其年，改封新安王，戶邑如先。

translations.literal: That same year he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an, his household fief as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year his title was changed to Prince of Xin'an with the same fief as before.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷北中郎將、南徐州刺史，領南琅邪太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Northern Central Army General and Governor of Southern Xu, concurrently serving as Governor of Southern Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was reassigned as Northern Central Army General and Governor of Southern Xu, while also serving as Governor of Southern Langye.

sentences.zh: 母殷淑儀，寵傾後宮，子鸞愛冠諸子，凡為上所盼遇者，莫不入子鸞之府、國。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Yin Shuyi enjoyed favor that overwhelmed the inner palace; Zi Luan's affection surpassed all the other sons; whatever the Emperor favored all entered Zi Luan's residence and fief.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Yin Shuyi enjoyed unrivaled favor in the inner palace. Zi Luan was more beloved than any of his brothers, and whatever the Emperor favored was given to Zi Luan's household and fief.

sentences.zh: 及為南徐州，又割吳郡以屬之。

translations.literal: When he became Governor of Southern Xu, Wu commandery was again carved out and made subject to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Governor of Southern Xu, Wu commandery was also detached and placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 六年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 追進淑儀為貴妃，班亞皇后，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Lady Shuyi was posthumously advanced to Noble Consort, ranking just below the empress, with the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shuyi was posthumously elevated to Noble Consort, ranking just below the empress, with the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 葬給轀輬車，虎賁、班劍，鑾輅九旒，黃屋左纛，前後部羽葆、鼓吹。

translations.literal: For the burial there were granted a funeral carriage, Tiger Guards, ceremonial swords, an imperial carriage with nine tassels, a yellow canopy with left banner, front and rear feathered parasols, and martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Her funeral was granted a funeral carriage, Tiger Guards, ceremonial swords, an imperial carriage with nine tassels, a yellow canopy with the left banner, feathered parasols before and behind, and martial music.

sentences.zh: 上自臨南掖門，臨過喪車，悲不自勝，左右莫不感動。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself went to the Southern Yeb Gate, watched the funeral carriage pass, and was overcome with grief; none at his side failed to be moved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went in person to the Southern Yeb Gate to watch the funeral carriage pass. He was overcome with grief, and all those around him were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 上痛愛不已，擬漢武李夫人賦，其詞曰：

translations.literal: The Emperor's anguished love would not cease; he modeled his words on Emperor Wu of Han's Rhapsody on Lady Li, saying:
translations.idiomatic: His grief and love would not subside. He composed a piece modeled on Emperor Wu of Han's Rhapsody on Lady Li, which reads:

sentences.zh: :朕以亡事棄日，閱覽前王詞苑，見李夫人賦，悽其有懷，亦以嗟詠久之，因感而會焉。

translations.literal: We, having cast away the day in idleness, perused the gardens of verse left by former kings and saw the Rhapsody on Lady Li; its poignant feeling struck home, and we too sighed and chanted it long, then composed in accord with that stirring.
translations.idiomatic: Having idled away the day, I browsed the verse collections of former kings and came upon the Rhapsody on Lady Li. Its poignant feeling struck home, and I sighed over it at length before composing in response to that stirring.

sentences.zh: :巡靈周之殘冊，略鴻漢之遺篆。

translations.literal: We toured the remnant registers of numinous Zhou and skimmed the surviving seal-script of vast Han.
translations.idiomatic: I toured the remnant chronicles of numinous Zhou and skimmed the surviving records of vast Han.

sentences.zh: 弔新宮之奄映，喭璧臺之蕪踐。

translations.literal: We mourned the new palace's sudden dimming and lamented the jade terrace's overgrown trampling.
translations.idiomatic: I mourned the new palace suddenly dimmed and lamented the jade terrace overgrown and trodden underfoot.

sentences.zh: 賦流波以謠思，詔河濟以崇典。

translations.literal: We composed on flowing waves to voice longing and proclaimed the Yellow and Ji to exalt ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: I composed on flowing waves to voice my longing and invoked the Yellow River and the Ji to exalt ritual precedent.

sentences.zh: 雖媛德之有載，竟滯悲其何遣。

translations.literal: Though fair virtue was recorded, in the end grief lingered—how could it be sent away?
translations.idiomatic: Though her fair virtue was recorded in history, in the end my grief lingered with no way to send it away.

sentences.zh: 訪物運之榮落，訊雲霞之舒卷。

translations.literal: We inquired into things' fate in glory and decline and questioned how cloud and mist spread and roll up.
translations.idiomatic: I inquired into the glory and decline of worldly fortune and pondered how cloud and mist spread and roll away.

sentences.zh: 念桂枝之秋霣，惜瑤華之春翦。

translations.literal: We thought on the cassia branch falling in autumn and grieved the jade blossom clipped in spring.
translations.idiomatic: I thought on the cassia branch falling in autumn and grieved the jade blossom cut down in spring.

sentences.zh: 桂枝折兮沿歲傾，瑤華碎兮思聯情。

translations.literal: The cassia branch breaks—along the years it topples; the jade blossom shatters—longing binds the feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The cassia branch breaks, and the years topple with it; the jade blossom shatters, and longing binds my heart.

sentences.zh: 彤殿閉兮素塵積，翠戺蕪兮紫苔生。

translations.literal: The crimson hall is shut—plain dust gathers; the green threshold is overgrown—purple moss grows.
translations.idiomatic: The crimson hall is shut, and plain dust gathers; the green threshold lies overgrown, and purple moss spreads.

sentences.zh: 寶羅暍兮春幌垂，珍簟空兮夏幬扃。

translations.literal: Precious gauze is stilled—the spring curtain hangs; the fine mat is empty—the summer screen is barred.
translations.idiomatic: Precious gauze lies still, the spring curtain hanging; the fine mat stands empty, the summer screen barred shut.

sentences.zh: 秋臺惻兮碧煙凝，冬宮冽兮朱火清。

translations.literal: The autumn terrace is mournful—azure mist congeals; the winter palace is chill—the vermilion flame is clear.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn terrace is mournful, azure mist congealing; the winter palace is chill, the vermilion flame burning clear.

sentences.zh: 流律有終，深心無歇。

translations.literal: Flowing seasons have an end; the deep heart knows no rest.
translations.idiomatic: The turning seasons have their end, but the deep heart knows no rest.

sentences.zh: 徙倚雲日，裴回風月。

translations.literal: We lingered by cloud and sun and wandered round with wind and moon.
translations.idiomatic: I lingered beneath cloud and sun and wandered with wind and moon.

sentences.zh: 思玉步於鳳墀，想金聲於鸞闕。

translations.literal: We thought on jade steps at the phoenix terrace and recalled golden voice at the luan gate-tower.
translations.idiomatic: I thought on her jade steps at the phoenix terrace and recalled her golden voice at the luan gate-tower.

sentences.zh: 竭方池而飛傷，損圜淵而流咽。

translations.literal: We drained the square pool in soaring grief and diminished the round abyss in flowing choked sobs.
translations.idiomatic: I drained the square pool with soaring grief and choked my sobs at the round abyss.

sentences.zh: 端蚤朝之晨罷，泛輦路之晚清。

translations.literal: We attended the early-morning court's dawn close and drifted along the imperial road in late clear dusk.
translations.idiomatic: I attended the dawn close of the early court and drifted along the imperial road in late clear dusk.

sentences.zh: 轥南陸，蹕閶闔，轢北津，警承明。

translations.literal: The wheels rolled over the southern causeway, the procession halted at Changhe Gate, crushed the northern ford, and alerted Chengming.
translations.idiomatic: The wheels rolled over the southern causeway, the procession halted at Changhe Gate, passed the northern ford, and alerted Chengm ing Palace.

sentences.zh: 面縞館之酸素，造松帳之葱青。

translations.literal: We faced the white mourning lodge's sour plainness and came to the pine canopy's verdant green.
translations.idiomatic: I faced the white mourning lodge in its stark plainness and came to the pine canopy in verdant green.

sentences.zh: 俛眾胤而慟興，撫藐女而悲生。

translations.literal: We bowed to the many descendants and grief rose; we stroked the tiny daughter and sorrow was born.
translations.idiomatic: I bowed to his many descendants and grief rose; I stroked his tiny daughter and sorrow was born anew.

sentences.zh: 雖哀終其已切，將何慰於爾靈。

translations.literal: Though mourning at the end was already keen, what could comfort your spirit?
translations.idiomatic: Though my mourning at the end was already keen, what could comfort your spirit?

sentences.zh: 存飛榮於景路，沒申藻於服車。

translations.literal: In life, soaring glory on the bright road; in death, extending elegiac ornament on the funeral carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In life she bore soaring glory on the bright road; in death elegiac ornament extends upon the funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 垂葆旒於昭術，竦鸞劍於清都。

translations.literal: Feathered tassels hung on the luminous avenue; luan swords stood tall in the pure capital.
translations.idiomatic: Feathered tassels hung along the luminous avenue; luan swords stood tall in the pure capital.

sentences.zh: 朝有儷於徵準，禮無替於粹圖。

translations.literal: At court she had her pair at the marked standard; in ritual none replaced her in the pure design.
translations.idiomatic: At court she had her place at the marked standard; in ritual none could replace her in the pure design.

sentences.zh: 閟瑤光之密陛，宮虛梁之餘陰。

translations.literal: The jade radiance of the secret steps was shut; the palace stood empty under the beam's remaining shade.
translations.idiomatic: The jade radiance of the secret steps was shut away; the palace stood empty beneath the beam's lingering shade.

sentences.zh: 俟玉羊之晨照，正金雞之夕臨。

translations.literal: We awaited the jade ram's morning shine and aligned the golden cock's evening approach.
translations.idiomatic: I awaited the jade ram's morning shine and aligned the golden cock's evening approach.

sentences.zh: 升雲鼛以引思，鏘鴻鐘以節音。

translations.literal: We raised the cloud drum to draw forth thought and rang the great bell to mark the tones.
translations.idiomatic: I raised the cloud drum to draw forth my thoughts and rang the great bell to mark the tones.

sentences.zh: 文七星於霜野，旗二燿於寒林。

translations.literal: We patterned the Seven Stars on the frosted wilds and bannered the Two Luminaries in the cold woods.
translations.idiomatic: I patterned the Seven Stars on the frosted wilds and raised banners to the Two Luminaries in the cold woods.

sentences.zh: 中雲枝之夭秀，寓坎泉之曾岑。

translations.literal: Centered was the cloud branch's early bloom, lodged in the pit spring's layered heights.
translations.idiomatic: Centered was the cloud branch in early bloom, lodged in the layered heights of the pit spring.

sentences.zh: 屈封嬴之自古，申反周乎在今。

translations.literal: We bent the enfeoffment of Ying from antiquity and declared the return to Zhou in the present.
translations.idiomatic: I bent the enfeoffment of Ying from antiquity and declared the return to Zhou in the present day.

sentences.zh: 遣雙靈兮達孝思，附孤魂兮展慈心。

translations.literal: We sent the paired spirits to convey filial thought and attached the lone soul to unfold compassionate heart.
translations.idiomatic: I sent the paired spirits to convey filial devotion and attached the lone soul to unfold compassionate care.

sentences.zh: 伊鞠報之必至，諒顯晦之同深。

translations.literal: Surely the offering's return must come; we trust that manifest and hidden share the same depth.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the offering's return must come; I trust that manifest and hidden share the same depth.

sentences.zh: 予棄西楚之齊化，略東門之遙䘳。

translations.literal: We abandoned the western Chu in its Qi transformation and sketched the eastern gate's distant mourning garment.
translations.idiomatic: I abandoned the western Chu in its Qi transformation and sketched the eastern gate's distant mourning garment.

sentences.zh: 淪漣兩拍之傷，奄抑七萃之箴。

translations.literal: Rippling grief in two beats, suddenly repressed the seven hosts' admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Rippling grief in two beats, suddenly repressing the seven hosts' admonition.

sentences.zh: 又諷有司曰：「典禮云，天子有后，有夫人。

translations.literal: He also admonished the responsible offices, saying: "The Ceremonial Canon says: the Son of Heaven has a queen and has ladies.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed the responsible offices: "The Ceremonial Canon states that the Son of Heaven has a queen and has consorts.

sentences.zh: 檀弓云，舜葬蒼梧，三妃不從。

translations.literal: The Zuo Tradition on the Sandalwood Bow says: when Shun was buried at Cangwu, the three consorts did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Tradition on the Sandalwood Bow records that when Shun was buried at Cangwu, his three consorts did not accompany the funeral.

sentences.zh: 昏義云，后立六宮，有三夫人。

translations.literal: The Meaning of Marriage says: the queen establishes the six palaces and has three ladies.
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of Marriage states that the queen establishes the six palaces and has three senior consorts.

sentences.zh: 然則三妃則三夫人也。

translations.literal: Thus the three consorts are the three ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the three consorts are the three senior ladies.

sentences.zh: 后之有三妃，猶天子之有三公也。

translations.literal: The queen's having three consorts is like the Son of Heaven's having three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The queen's three consorts correspond to the Son of Heaven's three dukes.

sentences.zh: 按周禮，三公八命，諸侯七命。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, the three dukes receive eight investitures, feudal lords seven.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Rites of Zhou, the three dukes receive eight investitures and feudal lords receive seven.

sentences.zh: 三公既尊於列國諸侯，三妃亦貴於庶邦夫人。

translations.literal: Since the three dukes are honored above the feudal lords of the various states, the three consorts are also noble above the ladies of common states.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the three dukes rank above the feudal lords of the various states, the three consorts rank above the principal ladies of ordinary states.

sentences.zh: 據春秋傳，仲子非魯惠公之元嫡，尚得考彼別宮；

translations.literal: According to the Spring and Autumn Annals tradition, Zhongzi was not Duke Hui of Lu's primary consort, yet still received sacrifice in a separate shrine;
translations.idiomatic: According to the Spring and Autumn tradition, although Zhongzi was not Duke Hui of Lu's primary consort, she still received sacrifice in a separate shrine;

sentences.zh: 今貴妃蓋天秩之崇班，理應創立新廟。

translations.literal: Now the Noble Consort is surely a lofty rank in Heaven's order and ought by right to have a new shrine established.
translations.idiomatic: The Noble Consort now holds a lofty rank in Heaven's order and ought by right to have a new shrine established for her.

sentences.zh: 」尚書左丞徐爰之又議：「宣貴妃既加殊命，禮絕五宮，考之古典，顯有成據。

translations.literal: " Left Director of the Secretariat Xu Aizhi further argued: "Since Consort Xuan has received an extraordinary appointment, her ritual stands apart from the five palaces; examining ancient models, there is clear precedent.
translations.idiomatic: " Left Director of the Secretariat Xu Aizhi further argued: "Since Consort Xuan has received an extraordinary appointment, her ritual stands apart from the five palaces. Examining ancient precedent, the case is clear.

sentences.zh: 廟堂克構，宜選將作大匠卿。」

translations.literal: The shrine hall can be completed; the Director of Works should be chosen."
translations.idiomatic: The shrine can be built; the Director of Works should be appointed."

sentences.zh: 葬畢，詔子鸞攝職，以本官兼司徒，進號撫軍、司徒，給鼓吹一部，禮儀並依正公。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete, an edict ordered Zi Luan to assume duties; with his existing office he concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat, was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army and Director of the Secretariat, was granted one set of martial music, and all ceremonial observances followed the orthodox duke.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, an edict ordered Zi Luan to assume his duties. He retained his existing office while concurrently serving as Director of the Secretariat, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and Director of the Secretariat, was granted a full ensemble of martial music, and all ceremonial observances followed those of an orthodox duke.

sentences.zh: 又加都督南徐州諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was also made Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed to command the armies of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 八年，加中書令，領司徒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Director of the Secretariat and headed the Secretariat as Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Director of the Secretariat while continuing to head that office.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，解中書令，領司徒，加持節之鎮。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor acceded, he was relieved of the Secretariat Directorship, headed the Secretariat as Director, and held a garrison with the Staff of Authority.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, Zi Luan was relieved of the Secretariat Directorship but retained the Secretariat as Director and held a garrison with the Staff of Authority.

sentences.zh: 帝素疾子鸞有寵，既誅羣公，乃遣使賜死，時年十歲。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long resented Zi Luan's favor; after he had executed the high ministers, he sent envoys to grant him death; he was then ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had long resented Zi Luan's favored status. After executing the high ministers, he sent envoys to order Zi Luan to take his own life. He was ten at the time.

sentences.zh: 子鸞臨死，謂左右曰：「願身不復生王家。

translations.literal: Facing death, Zi Luan said to those at his side: "I wish never to be born again into a royal house."
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Zi Luan said to those beside him: "I wish never to be born again into a royal house."

sentences.zh: 」同生弟妹並死，仍葬京口。

translations.literal: His younger siblings by the same mother all died as well and were buried at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger siblings by the same mother were also put to death and buried at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，詔曰：「夫紓寃申痛，雖往必追，緣情惻愛，感事彌遠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, an edict said: "To ease wrongs and voice pain—even the past must be pursued; moved by affection's tender love, one is stirred by events ever more distant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he issued an edict: "To ease wrongs and voice grief—even the past must be pursued. Moved by tender affection, one is stirred by events ever more distant.

sentences.zh: 故使持節、都督南徐州諸軍事、撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞，夙表成器，蚤延殊寵，方樹美業，克光蕃維。

translations.literal: Therefore the late Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Southern Xu, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Southern Xu, Xin'an Prince Zi Luan, from youth showed himself a finished vessel, early received extraordinary favor, was just raising fine achievement, and could have glorified the frontier screen.
translations.idiomatic: The late Bearer of the Staff of Authority Xin'an Prince Zi Luan, who commanded the armies of Southern Xu as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Southern Xu, showed promise from youth, received extraordinary favor early on, was just beginning to build a fine record, and could have brought glory to the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 而凶心肆忌，奄羅橫禍，興言永傷，有兼常懷，宜旍夭秀，以雪沈魂。

translations.literal: Yet a vicious heart indulged jealousy, suddenly ensnared him in calamity; to speak of it wounds forever, exceeding ordinary grief; he should be bannered in early bloom to cleanse the sunken soul.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a vicious heart indulged jealousy and suddenly engulfed him in calamity. To speak of it wounds forever, beyond ordinary grief. Let his early promise be honored with banners to cleanse his sunken soul.

sentences.zh: 可贈使持節、侍中、都督南徐兗二州諸軍事、司徒、南徐州刺史，王如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, command of the military affairs of Southern Xu and Yan, Director of the Secretariat, and Governor of Southern Xu; his princedom is unchanged."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously granted the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, command of Southern Xu and Yan, the Secretariat Directorship, and the governorship of Southern Xu, with his princedom unchanged."

sentences.zh: 第十二皇女、第二十二皇子子師，俱嬰謬酷，有增酸悼，皇女可贈縣公主，子師復先封為南海王，並加徽諡。

translations.literal: The twelfth imperial daughter and the twenty-second prince Zi Shi both met cruel wrong; grief was increased; the imperial daughter may be posthumously granted County Grand Princess; Zi Shi, who had earlier been enfeoffed as Prince of Nanhai, should both receive honorific posthumous titles."
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth imperial daughter and the twenty-second prince Zi Shi both suffered cruel wrong, deepening our grief. The imperial daughter may be posthumously granted the title County Grand Princess. Zi Shi, previously enfeoffed as Prince of Nanhai, and both shall receive honorific posthumous titles."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「哀枉追遠，仁道所弘，興滅繼絕，盛典斯貴。

translations.literal: It also said: "To pity the wronged and pursue the distant is what humaneness promotes; to raise what perished and continue what was cut off is the grand ceremony most honored.
translations.idiomatic: The edict also stated: "To pity the wronged and honor the distant is the path of humaneness. To restore what perished and continue what was cut off is the grand ceremony most honored.

sentences.zh: 朕務古思治，恩禮必敷，異族猶敦，況在近戚。

translations.literal: We devote ourselves to antiquity and think on good order; favor and ritual must be spread; even alien peoples are treated generously—how much more near kin.
translations.idiomatic: We devote ourselves to antiquity and seek good order. Favor and ritual must be extended generously—even to foreign peoples—how much more to close kin.

sentences.zh: 故新除使持節、侍中、都督南徐兗二州諸軍事、司徒、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞，年雖沖弱，性識早茂，鍾慈世祖，冠寵列蕃。

translations.literal: Therefore the newly removed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Southern Xu and Yan, Director of the Secretariat, and Governor of Southern Xu, Xin'an Prince Zi Luan, though young and tender in years, showed early maturity in nature and understanding, received the late Emperor's affection, and stood foremost in favor among the feudal princes.
translations.idiomatic: The late Xin'an Prince Zi Luan, recently granted the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, command of Southern Xu and Yan, the Secretariat Directorship, and the governorship of Southern Xu, was young in years but showed early maturity. He received Emperor Xiaowu's affection and stood foremost in favor among the feudal princes.

sentences.zh: 值景和凶虐，橫羅酷禍，國胤無主，寃祀莫寄，尋念痛悼，夙軫于懷。

translations.literal: He encountered the vicious cruelty of Jinghe, was suddenly ensnared in harsh calamity; the imperial heir had no master, grievance offerings had nowhere to rest; to recall it pains and mourns, long weighing on the heart.
translations.idiomatic: He met the vicious cruelty of the Jinghe reign and was suddenly engulfed in harsh calamity. The imperial heir was left without support, and grievance offerings had nowhere to rest. To recall it pains us still, long weighing on our heart.

sentences.zh: 可以建平王景素息延延年字德沖，泰始四年薨，時年四歲，諡曰沖王。

translations.literal: Prince of Jianping Jing Su's son Yan Yan, style Dechong, may be appointed; in the fourth year of Taishi he died, aged four; his posthumous title was Prince Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jianping Jing Su's son Yan Yan, whose style name was Dechong, may succeed him. He died in the fourth year of Taishi at age four and received the posthumous title Prince Chong.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以長沙王纂子延之為始平王，紹子鸞後。

translations.literal: The following year, Prince of Changsha Zuan's son Yan Zhi was again made Prince of Shiping to continue Zi Luan's line.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Prince of Changsha Zuan's son Yan Zhi was made Prince of Shiping to continue Zi Luan's line.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明三年薨，國除。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming under Emperor Shun he died and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 永嘉王

translations.literal: Prince of Yongjia
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yongjia

sentences.zh: 永嘉王子仁字孝和，孝武帝第九子也。

translations.literal: Yongjia Prince Zi Ren, style Xiaohe, was the ninth son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia Prince Zi Ren, whose style name was Xiaohe, was Emperor Xiaowu's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 大明五年，年五歲，監雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵隨二郡諸軍事、北中郎將、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，封永嘉王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming, at age five, he supervised the military affairs of the four provinces Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, and Southern Qin and the two commanderies Jingling and Sui of Yingzhou, as Northern Central Army General, Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians, and Governor of Yong; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongjia with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming, when he was five, he was appointed to supervise Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, and Southern Qin, along with Yingzhou's Jingling and Sui, with the titles Northern Central Army General, Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians, and Governor of Yong, and was made Prince of Yongjia with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 仍遷東中郎將、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He was also transferred to Eastern Central Army General and Governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was simultaneously reassigned as Eastern Central Army General and Governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 六年，又遷丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again transferred to Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was reassigned as Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 七年，兼衞尉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he concurrently served as Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he concurrently served as Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，加征虜將軍，領衞尉，丹陽尹如故。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor acceded, he was made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, headed the Commandant of the Guards, and his Intendancy of Danyang was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, retained the Commandant of the Guards, and kept his post as Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 尋出為左將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as General of the Left and Governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned as General of the Left and Governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，遷南徐州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he was transferred to Governor of Southern Xu; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe he was reassigned as Governor of Southern Xu while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 泰始元年，又遷中軍將軍，領太常。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi he was again transferred to Central Army General and headed the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taishi he was reassigned as Central Army General and concurrently as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未拜，徙護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before he could receive the appointment he was moved to General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the post he was reassigned as General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 四方平定，以為使持節、都督湘廣交三州諸軍事、平南將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: When the four quarters were pacified, he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the three provinces Xiang, Guang, and Jiao, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the realm was pacified, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority to command Xiang, Guang, and Jiao, with the titles General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣主書趙扶公宣旨於子仁曰：「汝一家門戶不建，幾覆社稷。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Chief Clerk Zhao Fugong to proclaim the imperial will to Zi Ren, saying: "Your whole house failed to establish itself and nearly overturned the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Chief Clerk Zhao Fugong to proclaim the imperial will to Zi Ren: "Your whole house failed to establish itself and nearly overturned the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 天未亡宋，景命集我。

translations.literal: Heaven has not yet destroyed Song; the bright mandate gathers upon me.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has not yet abandoned Song; the bright mandate rests upon me.

sentences.zh: 上流迷愚相扇，四海同惡，若非我修德御天下，三祖基業，一朝墜地，汝輩便應淪於異族之手。

translations.literal: The upper streams deluded and foolish fanned one another, the four seas shared the same evil; if not for our cultivating virtue to rule the realm, the foundation of the three ancestors would in one morning fall to earth, and you would fall into the hands of alien peoples.
translations.idiomatic: The upper Yangzi provinces deluded one another in folly, and the realm shared a common evil. Had I not cultivated virtue to rule the realm, the foundation laid by our three ancestors would have collapsed in a single morning, and you would have fallen into the hands of foreign peoples.

sentences.zh: 我昔兄弟近二十人，零落相繼，存者無幾。

translations.literal: We once had nearly twenty brothers; they fell away one after another, and few remain.
translations.idiomatic: I once had nearly twenty brothers. They have fallen away one after another, and few remain.

sentences.zh: 唯司徒年長，令德作輔，皇家門戶所憑，唯我與司徒二人而已，尚未能厭百姓姦心，餘諸王亦未堪贊治。

translations.literal: Only the Director of the Secretariat is eldest, with fine virtue as aide; upon whom the royal house's gate relies—only the two of us, the Director and myself; we have not yet been able to satisfy the people's treacherous hearts, and the remaining princes are also not fit to assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Director of the Secretariat is the elder, a man of fine virtue who supports the throne. The royal house depends on the two of us alone. We have not yet been able to quiet the people's treacherous hearts, and the remaining princes are not fit to assist in governance.

sentences.zh: 我惟有太子一人，司徒世子，年又幼弱，桂陽、巴陵並未有繼體，正賴汝輩兄弟，相倚為強，庶使天下不敢闚覘王室。

translations.literal: We have only the crown prince; the Director's heir is still young and weak; Guiyang and Baling both lack successors to continue the line; we rightly rely on you brothers to lean on one another for strength, so that perhaps the realm will not dare peep at the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: I have only the crown prince. The Director's heir is still young, and Guiyang and Baling both lack heirs. I rely on you brothers to support one another so that the realm will not dare cast covetous eyes on the royal house.

sentences.zh: 汝輩始十餘歲，裁知俛仰，當今諸舍細弱，殆不免人輕陵。

translations.literal: You are only just over ten years old and barely know how to bow and rise; today the various residences are delicate and weak and can hardly escape being lightly bullied by others.
translations.idiomatic: You are barely more than ten and scarcely know how to bow and rise. The various princely households are now weak and can hardly escape being bullied by others.

sentences.zh: 若非我為主，劉氏不辦今日。

translations.literal: If not for me as ruler, the house of Liu could not have achieved today.
translations.idiomatic: If I were not ruler, the house of Liu would not have survived to this day.

sentences.zh: 汝諸兄弟沖眇，為羣凶所逼誤，遂與百姓還圖骨肉，於汝在心，不得無愧。

translations.literal: You brothers are tender and small, forced and misled by the villainous band, and thus joined with the people to plot against kin; in your hearts you cannot be without shame.
translations.idiomatic: You brothers are young and tender, misled and driven by villains until you joined the people in plotting against your own kin. In your hearts you cannot be without shame.

sentences.zh: 即日四海就寧，恩化方始，方今處汝湘州。

translations.literal: From this day the four seas are at peace, gracious transformation is just beginning, and for now you are placed in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From this day the realm is at peace and gracious rule is just beginning. For now you are posted to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 汝年漸長，足知善惡，當每思刻厲，奉朝廷為心，爵秩自然與年俱進。

translations.literal: Your years gradually grow; you are fully able to know good and evil; you should always think on strict self-discipline, take serving the court as your heart, and rank and title will naturally advance with your years.
translations.idiomatic: As you grow older you will know good from evil. Always discipline yourself strictly, take serving the court as your guiding principle, and rank and title will naturally advance with your years.

sentences.zh: 我垂猶子之情，著於萬物；

translations.literal: Our affection as for a nephew is displayed in all things;
translations.idiomatic: My affection for you as a nephew is shown in all I do;

sentences.zh: 汝亦當知好，憶我敕旨。

translations.literal: you too should know what is good and remember my edict."
translations.idiomatic: and you too should know what is good and remember my edict."

sentences.zh: 」時司徒建安王休仁南討猶未還，既還白上，以將來非社稷計，宜並為之所。

translations.literal: At that time Director of the Secretariat Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren had not yet returned from the southern campaign; when he returned he reported to the Emperor that the future boded ill for the altars of state and that action should be taken against them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Director of the Secretariat Prince of Jian'an Xiu Ren had not yet returned from the southern campaign. When he returned he reported that these princes boded ill for the state and that action should be taken against them all.

sentences.zh: 未拜，賜死，時年十歲。

translations.literal: Before he could receive the appointment he was granted death; he was then ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume his post he was ordered to take his own life. He was ten at the time.

sentences.zh: 始安王

translations.literal: Prince of Shi'an
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shi'an

sentences.zh: 始安王子真字孝貞，孝武帝第十一子。

translations.literal: Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen, style Xiaozhen, was the eleventh son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an Prince Zi Zhen, whose style name was Xiaozhen, was Emperor Xiaowu's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 大明五年，年五歲，封始安王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming, at age five, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shi'an with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming, when he was five, he was made Prince of Shi'an with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 仍為輔國將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: He was also made General Who Assists the State and Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was simultaneously appointed General Who Assists the State and Governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷使持節、監廣交二州湘州之始興始安臨賀三郡諸軍事、平越中郎將、廣州刺史，將軍如故，不之鎮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, supervisor of the military affairs of the two provinces Guang and Jiao and the three commanderies Shixing, Shi'an, and Linhe of Xiangzhou, Central Army General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Governor of Guangzhou; his generalship was unchanged; he did not go to the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was reassigned as Bearer of the Staff of Authority to supervise Guang and Jiao, along with Xiangzhou's Shixing, Shi'an, and Linhe, with the titles Central Army General Who Pacifies the Yue and Governor of Guangzhou, while retaining his rank as general. He did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍、南彭城太守，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Southern Pengcheng, and took charge of the garrison at Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Southern Pengcheng, and placed in charge of the garrison at Stone City.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，為丹陽尹，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he became Intendant of Danyang; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe he was appointed Intendant of Danyang while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 尋復為南兗州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Governor of Southern Yan; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned as Governor of Southern Yan while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，遷左將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi he was transferred to General of the Left and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi he was reassigned as General of the Left and Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 未拜，賜死，時年十歲。

translations.literal: Before he could receive the appointment he was granted death; he was then ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume his post he was ordered to take his own life. He was ten at the time.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shaoling

sentences.zh: 邵陵王子元字孝善，孝武帝第十三子也。
