translations.literal: Shaoling Prince Zi Yuan, style Xiaoshan, was the thirteenth son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoling Prince Zi Yuan, whose style name was Xiaoshan, was Emperor Xiaowu's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 大明六年，年五歲，封邵陵王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daming, at age five, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daming, when he was five, he was made Prince of Shaoling with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 八年，以為度支校尉、秦南沛二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Colonel of Revenue and Governor of the two commanderies Qin and Nanpei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Colonel of Revenue and Governor of Qin and Nanpei.

sentences.zh: 仍為冠軍將軍、南琅邪泰山二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was also made Champion General and Governor of the two commanderies Southern Langye and Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: He was simultaneously appointed Champion General and Governor of Southern Langye and Taishan.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，出為湘州刺史，將軍如故，未之鎮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he went out as Governor of Xiangzhou; his generalship was unchanged; he did not go to the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe he was sent out as Governor of Xiangzhou while retaining his rank as general. He did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 至尋陽，值晉安王子勛為逆，留不之鎮。

translations.literal: When he reached Xunyang, Jin'an Prince Zi Xun had rebelled; he remained and did not go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xunyang, Jin'an Prince Zi Xun had risen in rebellion, so he remained there and did not proceed to his post.

sentences.zh: 進號撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 事平，賜死，時年九歲。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was granted death; he was then nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed he was ordered to take his own life. He was nine at the time.

sentences.zh: 齊敬王

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Jing
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Jing

sentences.zh: 齊敬王子羽字孝英，孝武帝第十四子也。

translations.literal: Qi Jing Prince Zi Yu, style Xiaoying, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jing Prince Zi Yu, whose style name was Xiaoying, was Emperor Xiaowu's fourteenth son.

sentences.zh: 大明二年生，三年卒，追加封諡。

translations.literal: He was born in the second year of Daming and died in the third; enfeoffment and posthumous title were added retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the second year of Daming and died in the third. Enfeoffment and a posthumous title were granted retroactively.

sentences.zh: 淮南王

translations.literal: Prince of Huainan
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huainan

sentences.zh: 淮南王子孟字孝光，孝武帝第十六子也。

translations.literal: Huainan Prince Zi Meng, style Xiaoguang, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan Prince Zi Meng, whose style name was Xiaoguang, was Emperor Xiaowu's sixteenth son.

sentences.zh: 大明七年，年五歲，封淮南王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming, at age five, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huainan with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daming, when he was five, he was made Prince of Huainan with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時世祖改豫州之南梁郡為淮南國，罷南豫州之淮南郡并宣城。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor changed Southern Liang commandery of Yuzhou into the state of Huainan and abolished Huainan commandery of Southern Yuzhou, merging it with Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor changed Yuzhou's Southern Liang commandery into the state of Huainan and abolished Southern Yuzhou's Huainan commandery, merging it with Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，二郡並復舊，子孟仍國名度食淮南郡。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor acceded, both commanderies were restored to the old arrangement; Zi Meng still bore the state name and drew his sustenance from Huainan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, both commanderies were restored to their former status. Zi Meng retained the state name and drew his fief income from Huainan commandery.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，為冠軍將軍、南琅邪彭城二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he became Champion General and Governor of the two commanderies Southern Langye and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe he was appointed Champion General and Governor of Southern Langye and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，改封安成王，戶邑如先。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng, his household fief as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi his title was changed to Prince of Ancheng with the same fief as before.

sentences.zh: 未拜，賜死，時年八歲。

translations.literal: Before he could receive the appointment he was granted death; he was then eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume his post he was ordered to take his own life. He was eight at the time.

sentences.zh: 晉陵孝王

translations.literal: Prince of Jinling Xiao
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jinling Xiao

sentences.zh: 晉陵孝王子雲字孝舉，孝武帝第十九子也。

translations.literal: Jinling Xiao Prince Zi Yun, style Xiaoju, was the nineteenth son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling Xiao Prince Zi Yun, whose style name was Xiaoju, was Emperor Xiaowu's nineteenth son.

sentences.zh: 大明六年，年四歲，封晉陵王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daming, at age four, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jinling with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daming, when he was four, he was made Prince of Jinling with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 未拜，其年薨。

translations.literal: Before he could receive the appointment he died that same year.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume his post he died that same year.

sentences.zh: 南海王

translations.literal: Prince of Nanhai
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nanhai

sentences.zh: 南海哀王子師字孝友，孝武帝第二十二子也。

translations.literal: Nanhai Ai Prince Zi Shi, style Xiaoyou, was the twenty-second son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Nanhai Ai Prince Zi Shi, whose style name was Xiaoyou, was Emperor Xiaowu's twenty-second son.

sentences.zh: 大明七年，年四歲，封南海王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming, at age four, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanhai with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daming, when he was four, he was made Prince of Nanhai with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 未拜，景和元年，為前廢帝所害，時年六歲。

translations.literal: Before he could receive the appointment, in the first year of Jinghe he was killed by the Former Deposed Emperor; he was then six years old.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume his post, he was killed by the Former Deposed Emperor in the first year of Jinghe. He was six at the time.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，追諡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, a posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, a posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 淮陽王

translations.literal: Prince of Huaiyang
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huaiyang

sentences.zh: 淮陽思王子霄，字孝雲，孝武帝第二十三子也。

translations.literal: Huaiyang Si Prince Zi Xiao, style Xiaoyun, was the twenty-third son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyang Si Prince Zi Xiao, whose style name was Xiaoyun, was Emperor Xiaowu's twenty-third son.

sentences.zh: 大明五年生，八年薨，追加封諡。

translations.literal: He was born in the fifth year of Daming and died in the eighth; enfeoffment and posthumous title were added retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the fifth year of Daming and died in the eighth. Enfeoffment and a posthumous title were granted retroactively.

sentences.zh: 東平王

translations.literal: Prince of Dongping
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Dongping

sentences.zh: 東平王子嗣字孝叔，孝武帝第二十七子也。

translations.literal: Dongping Prince Zi Si, style Xiaoshu, was the twenty-seventh son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping Prince Zi Si, whose style name was Xiaoshu, was Emperor Xiaowu's twenty-seventh son.

sentences.zh: 大明七年生，仍封東平王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was born in the seventh year of Daming and was at once enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Born in the seventh year of Daming, he was at once made Prince of Dongping with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 繼東平沖王休倩。

translations.literal: He succeeded Dongping Chong Prince Xiu Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Dongping Chong Prince Xiu Qian as heir.

sentences.zh: 休倩母顏性理嚴酷，泰始二年，子嗣所生母景寧園昭容謝上表曰：「故東平沖王休倩託荄璿極，岐嶷夙表，降年弗永，遺胤莫傳。

translations.literal: Xiu Qian's mother Yan was by nature stern and cruel. In the second year of Taishi, Zi Si's birth mother, Lady Xie, Attendant of Jingning Garden, submitted a memorial, saying: "The late Dongping Chong Prince Xiu Qian was entrusted to the jade axis of the pole, showed early keen intelligence, but his descending years were not long and left no heir to transmit the line.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu Qian's mother Yan was by nature harsh and cruel. In the second year of Taishi, Zi Si's birth mother Lady Xie, Attendant of Jingning Garden, submitted a memorial: "The late Dongping Chong Prince Xiu Qian was entrusted to the imperial house, showed keen intelligence from youth, but died young and left no heir.

sentences.zh: 孝武皇帝敕妾子臣子嗣出繼為後，既承國祀，方奉烝薦，庶覃遐慶，式延于遠。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu ordered my son the subject Zi Si to go out in adoption as successor; having received the state's sacrifices, he was just offering the seasonal offerings, hoping to spread distant blessing and extend it far.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered my son Zi Si to be given in adoption as his successor. Having received the state's sacrifices, he was just beginning to offer the seasonal rites, hoping to spread blessing far into the future.

sentences.zh: 而妾顏訓養非恩，撫導乖理，情闕引進，義違負螟。

translations.literal: Yet the lady Yan's nurturing was not gracious, her guidance contrary to reason, affection lacking in advancement, duty violated like abandoning the locust larva.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lady Yan's nurturing was not kind, her guidance contrary to reason, her affection failing to nurture him, her conduct violating the duty owed to an adopted son.

sentences.zh: 昔世祖平日，詭申慈愛；

translations.literal: In former days, during the Emperor's ordinary times, she falsely displayed affection;
translations.idiomatic: In former days, during the Emperor's lifetime, she only pretended affection;

sentences.zh: 崩背未幾，真性便發，猶逼畏崇憲，少欲藏掩。

translations.literal: not long after his death her true nature burst forth, yet still constrained by fear of Empress Dowager Chongxian, she wished somewhat to conceal it.
translations.idiomatic: not long after his death her true nature emerged, yet still constrained by fear of Empress Dowager Chongxian, she tried somewhat to conceal it.

sentences.zh: 自茲以後，專縱嚴酷，實顯布宗戚，宣灼宮闈，用傷人倫，爰惻行路。

translations.literal: From then on she indulged solely in severity and cruelty, truly displaying it among the imperial kin, proclaiming it throughout the inner palace, thereby wounding human relations and moving passersby to pity.
translations.idiomatic: From then on she indulged solely in harsh cruelty, displaying it openly among the imperial kin and throughout the inner palace, wounding human decency and moving all who heard to pity.

sentences.zh: 妾天屬冥至，感切實深，伏願乾渥廣臨，曲垂照賜，復改命還依本屬，則妾母子雖隕之辰，猶生之年。

translations.literal: Your servant's heaven-bound kin has reached the dark realm; the feeling cuts truly deep. We prostrate ourselves hoping for broad imperial favor and bending grace, that the command be changed and he return to his original status; then for your servant mother and son, though the hour of falling, it would still be a day of life."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's kin has reached the dark realm, and my grief cuts deep. I prostrate myself hoping for your broad favor: change the command and let him return to his original status. Then for mother and son, though we face ruin, it would still be as though we lived."

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 其年賜死，時年四歲。

translations.literal: That year he was granted death; he was then four years old.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was ordered to take his own life. He was four at the time.

sentences.zh: 武陵王

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wuling

sentences.zh: 武陵王贊字仲敷，明帝第九子也。

translations.literal: Wuling Prince Zan, style Zhongfu, was the ninth son of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Wuling Prince Zan, whose style name was Zhongfu, was Emperor Ming's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年生。

translations.literal: He was born in the sixth year of Taishi.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the sixth year of Taishi.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔曰：「世祖孝武皇帝雖恃尊墯惠，勳狹政弛，樂飲無饜，事因於寧泰，任威縱費，義緣於務寡。

translations.literal: That year an edict said: "Although Emperor Xiaowu relied on honored rank and heaped favor, his achievements were narrow and governance lax, he delighted in drink without satiety, affairs arose from over-tranquility, he indulged authority and unrestrained expenditure, and righteousness was strained because duties were few.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict stated: "Although Emperor Xiaowu relied on his exalted rank and lavished favor, his achievements were narrow and governance lax. He delighted in drink without restraint. Affairs arose from excessive peace; he indulged authority and spent freely, and righteousness suffered because duties were neglected.

sentences.zh: 故以積怨動天，流殃胤嗣，景和肇釁，義嘉成禍，世祖繼體，陷憲無遺。

translations.literal: Therefore accumulated resentment moved Heaven, calamity flowed to his descendants, Jinghe began the strife, Yijia completed the disaster, and the heirs of the Emperor fell entirely under punishment with none spared.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore accumulated resentment moved Heaven, and calamity flowed to his descendants. Jinghe began the strife, Yijia completed the disaster, and the Emperor's heirs fell entirely under punishment with none spared.

sentences.zh: 昔皇家中圮，含生懼滅，賴英孝感奮，掃雪寃恥，勳纘墜歷，拯茲窮氓。

translations.literal: Formerly the imperial house was overthrown, all living beings feared extinction; relying on heroic filial feeling he rose in vigor, swept away the snow of grievance and shame, continued the fallen succession, and rescued these destitute people.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the imperial house was overthrown and all living beings feared extinction. Relying on heroic filial devotion he rose up, swept away grievance and shame, continued the fallen succession, and rescued the destitute people.

sentences.zh: 繼絕追遠，禮訓攸尚，況既帝且兄，而缺斯典。

translations.literal: To continue what was cut off and pursue the distant is what ritual teaching honors; how much more when he was both emperor and elder brother, yet this ceremony was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: To restore what was cut off and honor the distant is what ritual teaching esteems. How much more when he was both emperor and elder brother, yet this ceremony was lacking.

sentences.zh: 今以第九子智隨奉世祖為子，武陵郡大明之世，事均代邦，可封智隨武陵王，食邑五千戶。

translations.literal: Now the ninth son Zhi Sui is to serve Emperor Xiaowu as son; in the Daming era Wuling commandery's affairs equaled the domain of Dai; Zhi Sui may be enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling with a fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Now the ninth son Zhi Sui is to serve as Emperor Xiaowu's heir. In the Daming era Wuling commandery's standing equaled the domain of Dai. Zhi Sui may be enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling with a fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋世祖一門女累不少，既無釐總，義須防閑，諸侯雖不得祖稱天子，而事有一家之切。

translations.literal: Soon it was seen that the Emperor's house had no few daughters and female dependents; since there was no overall regulation, propriety required safeguards; though feudal lords may not address the Son of Heaven as ancestor, the matter has the urgency of one family.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon seen that the Emperor's house had many daughters and female dependents. Since there was no overall regulation, propriety required safeguards. Though feudal lords may not address the Son of Heaven as ancestor, the matter concerns the urgency of one family.

sentences.zh: 且歸寧有所，疹疾相營，得失是任，閨房有稟。

translations.literal: Moreover there are places for returning home in peace, ailments to tend for one another, gains and losses to be entrusted, and the inner quarters have their reports.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover there are visits home in peace, ailments to tend for one another, gains and losses to be entrusted, and matters reported from the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 朕應天在位，恩深九族，庶此足申追睦之懷，敷愛之旨。」

translations.literal: We, responding to Heaven on the throne, favor the nine kindreds deeply; we hope this suffices to express the feeling of pursuing kinship and spreading the intent of love."
translations.idiomatic: We, responding to Heaven on the throne, favor the nine kindreds deeply. We hope this suffices to express our pursuit of kinship and our intent to spread affection."

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽四年，出為使持節、督南徐兗青冀五州諸軍事、北中郎將、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor he went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, supervisor of the military affairs of the five provinces Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji, Northern Central Army General, and Governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority to supervise Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji, with the titles Northern Central Army General and Governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明元年，遷持節、督郢州司州之義陽諸軍事、前將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming under Emperor Shun he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of the military affairs of Yingzhou and Yiyang of Sizhou, Forward General, and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming under Emperor Shun he was reassigned as Bearer of the Staff to supervise Yingzhou and Sizhou's Yiyang, with the titles Forward General and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，為沈攸之所圍，徙都督荊湘雍益梁寧南北秦八州諸軍事、安西將軍、荊州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he was besieged by Shen Youzhi and was moved to Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the eight provinces Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, Northern Qin, and Southern Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Jingzhou; his Staff of Authority was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was besieged by Shen Youzhi and was reassigned to command Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, Northern Qin, and Southern Qin, with the titles General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jingzhou, while retaining the Staff of Authority.

sentences.zh: 攸之平，乃之鎮。

translations.literal: When Youzhi was pacified, he then went to his post.
translations.idiomatic: After Youzhi was suppressed, he then proceeded to his post.

sentences.zh: 其年薨，時年九歲，國除。

translations.literal: That year he died; he was then nine years old; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year at age nine, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: Historian's Comment
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Comment

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉安諸王，提挈羣下，以成其釁亂，遂至九域沸騰，難結天下，而世祖之胤亦殲焉。

translations.literal: The historian says: The Jin'an princes led their followers to accomplish their mutinous disorder, until the nine regions seethed and difficulty bound the realm, and the Emperor's descendants were also exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The Jin'an princes led their followers to accomplish their rebellion, until the nine regions seethed and turmoil gripped the realm, and the Emperor's descendants were also exterminated.

sentences.zh: 強不如弱，義在於此也。

translations.literal: Strong is not as good as weak—the principle lies herein.
translations.idiomatic: Strength is not as good as weakness—such is the principle.
